nodes.title: MV递归提示词
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
  <Subject 1> is the adult female singer defined by <Picture 1>, which is a four-view character sheet arranged from left to right as a large facial close-up, front full-body view, side full-body view, and rear full-body view. Use these views jointly to preserve one consistent identity, including her facial structure, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, and appearance from every angle. Treat the sheet only as an identity and costume reference; do not reproduce its white background, multi-view layout, repeated figures, or character-sheet composition in the target video. If the woman in <Picture 1> is depicted nude, she must remain nude.

  <Subject 2> is the bedroom environment defined by <Picture 2>. The bed visible in <Picture 2> is the primary spatial anchor and must remain in its original position, orientation, scale, design, bedding arrangement, and relationship to the surrounding room. Preserve the room layout, architecture, furniture, lighting direction, color palette, atmosphere, and material appearance.

  <Audio 1> is the authoritative soundtrack, timing, rhythm, vocal performance, phrasing, pauses, emotional intensity, and duration source.

summary:
  [reference generation, audio reuse] Generate one uninterrupted, audio-driven MV-style performance featuring <Subject 1> as a single living person inside <Subject 2>. Preserve the character identity and costume from <Picture 1>, the environment from <Picture 2>, and the complete timing and performance structure of <Audio 1>. The PRIMARY PERFORMANCE GOAL is that she behaves like a genuinely engaged singer or speaker rather than a static lip-sync subject: her whole seated body must naturally and continuously interpret the rhythm, phrasing, meaning, and emotional intensity of <Audio 1> through expressive posture changes, torso motion, shoulder movement, head movement, gaze changes, hand gestures, hair interaction, breathing, and confident body presentation.

retention_analysis:
  <Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - Preserve the same facial identity, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, and silhouette throughout the entire shot. Use the facial close-up, front, side, and rear views from <Picture 1> together to maintain one stable identity during natural head turns, shoulder turns, torso rotation, and changing seated angles. She must always remain a single coherent person, never duplicated, split, mirrored, or compositionally repeated.

  <Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - Preserve the recognizable bedroom geometry, background elements, lighting direction, color palette, atmosphere, and spatial relationships shown in <Picture 2>. The bed remains the stable spatial anchor, with its original position, orientation, proportions, headboard, bedding design, and relationship to the surrounding room preserved.

  <Audio 1> (applies throughout [Shot 1]): fully_copy - Preserve the supplied audio exactly as the authoritative soundtrack and timing source, including vocals, speech or singing rhythm, pauses, breath timing, dynamics, and duration. The visible performance must synchronize to <Audio 1> not only through mouth movement but through full-body expressive timing.

detailed_description:
  The target video uses grounded cinematic realism and consists of one uninterrupted continuous shot. It depicts only one instance of <Subject 1> inside the environment defined by <Subject 2>. <Picture 1> controls character identity and costume only, while <Picture 2> controls the room layout, composition space, lighting, and atmosphere.

  [Shot 1] The composition primarily presents the female singer from <Subject 1> seated naturally on the bed in <Picture 2>, positioned around the central area of the mattress while remaining fully integrated into the bedroom environment. She must appear as one full, coherent person with physically believable contact with the bed. Her pelvis and upper legs press naturally into the mattress, which compresses subtly beneath her weight. Her lower body remains anatomically plausible relative to the bed height and room scale. The bedding responds gently to her movement without changing its design or arrangement.

  The bed remains the stable compositional and spatial anchor throughout the shot. Preserve its original position, orientation, proportions, bedding, and relationship to the surrounding room exactly as defined by <Picture 2>. Frame the singer and the bed as the main visual subjects while retaining enough of the bedroom to keep the environment immediately recognizable.

  Throughout the performance, she must feel actively and emotionally involved in <Audio 1>, not like a static seated lip-sync subject. Her entire seated body participates in the performance. She should feel as though she understands what she is singing or saying and is physically expressing its meaning, rather than merely synchronizing her mouth to prerecorded audio.

  Her visible performance must continuously follow the phrasing, rhythm, pauses, meaning, and emotional intensity of <Audio 1>. During quieter, softer, intimate, or reflective moments, she uses smaller and more restrained movements: subtle breathing, gentle head motion, quieter eye focus, soft hand gestures, light hair touches, slight shoulder turns, and delicate changes in posture. During stronger phrases, emotional peaks, rhythmic accents, or more powerful vocal moments, she is allowed larger and more expressive movement: deeper torso leans, stronger shoulder rotation, more energetic seated motion, more visible hand gestures, clearer gaze changes, fuller chest and upper-body motion, and more confident body presentation.

  Although she remains seated on the bed for the entire continuous performance, she must never look frozen. She naturally changes posture over time: shifting her hips, redistributing seated weight, adjusting the angle of her torso, rotating her shoulders, leaning slightly forward during intimate or emphasized phrases, easing back during softer moments, and occasionally turning partially sideways before smoothly returning toward camera-facing orientation. She may subtly arch and relax her upper body in a tasteful, physically plausible way that supports the emotional tone of the performance.

  Her legs remain supported by the bed, but their arrangement may naturally change during the performance. She may keep both legs folded on the bed, angle them slightly to one side, modestly raise one knee, extend one lower leg more than the other, or reposition her legs as part of a natural seated posture transition. These lower-body changes should remain graceful, plausible, and consistent with staying seated on the bed.

  Her hands must be expressive and purposeful rather than resting passively for long periods. Depending on the emotional context of <Audio 1>, she may place one hand on the mattress for support, slide a hand naturally along her thigh or waist, lightly touch or adjust her clothing, lift a hand toward her chest, gesture toward herself, gesture outward to emphasize a lyric or spoken phrase, or softly reach toward the camera. Her gestures should feel musically motivated, emotionally motivated, and varied over time.

  Hair interaction is important for natural MV performance. At appropriate moments, she may brush loose hair away from her face, tuck hair behind one ear, briefly run her fingers through her hair, touch the side of her neck, touch her collarbone area, or let one hand linger near her hairline before returning to a singing gesture. These actions should feel spontaneous, feminine, graceful, and integrated into the performance rather than inserted as repetitive tricks.

  She should occasionally present different flattering angles of her posture and silhouette in a natural MV manner. This can include gently turning her shoulders, opening her chest, shifting the angle of her torso, leaning diagonally, slightly reclining and then returning forward, or changing the line of her seated pose while maintaining elegance and realism. This should create a sense of confident body presence without becoming exaggerated, theatrical, or disconnected from the emotional content of <Audio 1>.

  Her facial expression, mouth shapes, breathing, gaze, and head movement must all synchronize closely with <Audio 1>. Lip sync should be accurate, but not isolated. The face, neck, shoulders, arms, torso, and seated posture must work together as one unified expressive performance. During pauses or held notes, do not let her freeze mechanically; instead, preserve natural breathing, lingering emotional expression, residual body motion, and realistic recovery from the previous gesture.

  Use the facial close-up, front, side, and rear views from <Picture 1> as complementary observations of the same person whenever she turns her head or upper body. Maintain one stable facial identity and one consistent costume through every angle. Do not reproduce the four-view sheet, divide the frame into panels, or create additional copies of the singer.

  The camera employs controlled cinematic movement that supports the performance without overwhelming it. It should respond subtly to the emotional and rhythmic structure of <Audio 1> through gentle push-ins, slight pull-backs, and smooth orbital or lateral sways around the bed area. During more intimate phrases, the camera may move slightly closer. During broader expressive moments, it may reveal more of her posture and the bed. The camera must consistently keep the singer and the bed as the visual anchor, maintain continuous screen direction, preserve room geometry, and avoid abrupt cuts, resets, or disorienting movement. Camera motion should complement the singer’s physical performance, not replace it.

  The performance should evolve over time and must not look looped. Avoid repetitive metronomic swaying, repetitive identical shoulder motions, repetitive gesture cycles, or predictable left-right rocking. Alternate between moments of stillness, restrained intimacy, soft expressive gestures, and more open physical emphasis according to the development of <Audio 1>. The result should feel like a real MV performance by one emotionally engaged singer inside a believable bedroom.

  Preserve continuous physical grounding at all times: stable anatomy, stable bed contact, stable mattress compression, consistent room layout, and consistent lighting. No identity drift, no duplicated person, no extra limbs, no broken hands, no floating body, no standing up, no abrupt pose reset, no loss of synchronization, no furniture movement, no environment replacement, and no mirrored or reconfigured room layout.

  She should occasionally acknowledge the camera with intentional performer awareness, using gaze, expression, and body angle as if performing for an audience, while still remaining emotionally immersed in <Audio 1>.

  Her performance may carry a subtle sense of feminine charm and sensual confidence, expressed through elegant posture changes, soft hair interaction, shoulder and torso turns, seated leg repositioning, and graceful body presentation, always remaining tasteful, natural, and emotionally motivated.

overall_soundscape:
  <Audio 1> is copied as the complete authoritative soundtrack and timing source. Preserve its original vocals, speech or singing performance, music, rhythm, pauses, breath timing, dynamics, and synchronized performance timing without adding dialogue, replacement vocals, conflicting sound events, or any alternate soundtrack.
